title: Can LLMs Rank?
summary: Diagnosing whether LLM pairwise rankings can be trusted: consistency within a run and agreement across runs.

title: Budgeting Discretion
summary: Formalizing discretion as a finite override budget, with a dynamic threshold rule set by the tail-heaviness of potential gains, and evidence that caseworkers ration overrides against real capacity and timing.

title: Eviction Prediction Framework
summary: A modular, leakage-free pipeline for eviction-risk modeling, with strict temporal splits and pluggable feature generators as first-class objects.

title: Fixed Points and Stochastic Meritocracies
summary: How merit-based, individually fair selection can still entrench group inequality over time, once a small affinity feedback loop turns random early leads into self-reinforcing ones.

title: Street-Level AI
summary: Testing whether off-the-shelf LLMs can stand in for street-level bureaucrats in homelessness allocation; they prove internally inconsistent and poorly aligned with vetted vulnerability scores.

title: Discretionary Trees
summary: Using machine learning to make street-level discretion in homelessness services legible, showing that discretionary overrides are targeted and welfare-improving rather than arbitrary.

title: Two-Sided Bandits in Matching Markets
summary: Decentralized algorithms that provably converge to stable matchings when both sides of a market must learn their preferences and cannot communicate.

title: Increasing the Value of Information in Online POMDP Planning
summary: An entropy-augmented UCB rule for POMCP that keeps online planners from undervaluing information gathering when its payoff is delayed.
